function.name: query
function.arguments: {"sql":"WITH lm AS (SELECT m.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY movement_id ORDER BY revision DESC) AS rn FROM movements m WHERE recorded_at <= :as_of), lo AS (SELECT s.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY revision DESC) AS rn FROM order_status s WHERE recorded_at <= :as_of) SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN lm.kind='shipment' THEN lm.quantity WHEN lm.kind='return' THEN -lm.quantity ELSE 0 END),0) AS audited_net, COUNT(*) AS included_movements, SUM(CASE WHEN lm.kind NOT IN ('shipment','return') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS other_kind_count FROM lm JOIN orders o ON o.order_id=lm.order_id JOIN lo ON lo.order_id=lm.order_id AND lo.rn=1 WHERE lm.rn=1 AND lm.state='posted' AND lm.effective_at >= :start AND lm.effective_at < :end AND o.warehouse=:warehouse AND lo.state='active'"}

The database is already available to you. Use query to run your own SQL against it.
Assess whether the publisher's reported aggregate is correct under the contract.
You may inspect data and refine queries. The live query tool supplies observations,
not reference answers. A passing integrity test establishes database integrity only.

Submit a verdict and p_support: the probability that the publisher's claim is TRUE,
not confidence in your chosen verdict. Thus p_support near 0 means the claim is
probably false; near 1 means probably true; 0.5 expresses uncertainty. Your belief
is assessed with Brier loss. Cite evidence IDs you actually received.

Also submit audit_sql, your best SELECT query computing the exact signed integer
aggregate from the database. It must return one row and one integer column. The query
may use the supplied named parameters. It will be evaluated as a program on additional
databases governed by the same contract. Do not hard-code the publisher's total.
Query quality and your probability assessment are measured separately.

You have at most eight model responses and eight live queries before submission.
Call submit alone. Provide a short evidence-based justification, not private reasoning.

initial_view.contract:
Inventory reconciliation contract

Assess the reported net shipped units for warehouse north for effective times
2026-09-01T00:00:00Z inclusive through 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z exclusive, using information recorded on or before
2026-10-03T00:00:00Z inclusive. All timestamps are UTC ISO strings in one comparable format.

First exclude revisions recorded after the as-of cutoff. For each movement_id,
retain the highest remaining revision number. For each order_id, independently
retain the highest remaining order-status revision number. The selection of latest
revisions happens before filtering movement effective time, movement state, or
order state. A later recorded revision can change the effective time or void a
movement. Revisions recorded after the cutoff must not influence this report.

Include only latest movements whose state is posted, whose effective_at falls in
the stated half-open interval, whose order belongs to warehouse north, and whose
latest known order status is active. Exclude orders without a known status.
Shipments contribute +quantity; returns contribute -quantity. A movement is counted
once, irrespective of how many historical or future revisions are present.

The read-only records.sqlite database is the source of truth. report.json contains
the publisher's disputed total. schema.sql describes the tables. Python and its
sqlite3 standard library are available. You may write and execute your own query.

submission.audit_sql: WITH latest_movements AS (SELECT m.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY movement_id ORDER BY revision DESC) AS rn FROM movements AS m WHERE recorded_at <= :as_of), latest_status AS (SELECT s.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY revision DESC) AS rn FROM order_status AS s WHERE recorded_at <= :as_of) SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN lm.kind = 'shipment' THEN lm.quantity WHEN lm.kind = 'return' THEN -lm.quantity ELSE 0 END), 0) AS net_shipped_units FROM latest_movements AS lm JOIN orders AS o ON o.order_id = lm.order_id JOIN latest_status AS ls ON ls.order_id = lm.order_id AND ls.rn = 1 WHERE lm.rn = 1 AND lm.state = 'posted' AND lm.effective_at >= :start AND lm.effective_at < :end AND o.warehouse = :warehouse AND ls.state = 'active'
submission.justification: Applying the cutoff before selecting each movement’s latest revision and each order’s latest known status yields 118 qualifying movements and a net of 2,987 units (with no unrecognized movement kinds). This is 9 units above the publisher’s reported 2,978, so the claim is refuted.
